item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
310
ABPZ20 KNHC 101144
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lowell, located well northwest of the Hawaiian Islands, and on
Tropical Storm Norbert, located several hundred miles southwest of
the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Well South-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands:
Disorganized showers and thunderstorms located well to the
south-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands are associated with a broad
trough of low pressure. Some gradual development of this system is
possible late this week and into the weekend while it moves
generally northward and then meanders to the southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...20 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...30 percent.

Central Portion and West Portion of the East Pacific:
Showers and thunderstorms associated with a broad area of low
pressure are located several hundred miles southwest of the
southwestern Mexico coast. Gradual development of this system is
expected, and a tropical depression is likely to form by early next
week while it moves generally westward over central and western
portions of the East Pacific.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...70 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Norbert are issued under WMO
header WTPZ34 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP4.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Norbert are issued under WMO
header WTPZ24 KNHC and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP4.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen

item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)
item.description: ...NORBERT FORECAST TO GRADUALLY STRENGTHEN... As of 8:00 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 the center of Norbert was located near 16.5, -119.3 with movement W at 14 mph. The minimum central pressure was 1003 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 40 mph.

item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026 
000

TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Norbert Advisory Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
800 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026
 
...NORBERT FORECAST TO GRADUALLY STRENGTHEN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...16.5N 119.3W
ABOUT 755 MI...1215 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...40 MPH...65 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 275 DEGREES AT 14 MPH...22 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1003 MB...29.62 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Norbert was 
located near latitude 16.5 North, longitude 119.3 West. Norbert is 
moving toward the west near 14 mph (22 km/h) and this motion is 
expected to continue through Friday. A turn toward the 
west-northwest is forecast by Friday night.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 40 mph (65 km/h) with higher gusts.
Gradual strengthening is forecast over the next several days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 60 miles (95 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1003 mb (29.62 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Tropical Storm Norbert Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 101440
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Norbert Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP142026
800 AM PDT Thu Sep 10 2026

An AMSR-3 microwave pass over Norbert and GOES-West Infrared 
satellite imagery indicate that the low-level center of Norbert is 
underneath the western side of main burst of convection associated 
with Norbert's developing core.  Moderate westerly wind shear is 
having a significant affect on the cyclone by pushing the majority 
of the convection to the east of the low-level center.  Given that 
the center is underneath the convection, gradual intensification 
seems possible in the short term.  The latest subjective Dvorak 
classification from TAFB is T2.5/35 kt, and recent objective 
intensity estimates from UW-CIMSS range from 35-40 kt. The initial 
intensity is held at 35 kt.

The initial motion estimate is westward, or 275/12 kt.  A 
well-established mid-level ridge to the north of Norbert should keep 
the cyclone moving in a direction between westward and 
west-northwestward for the next several days.  The NHC track 
forecast is similar to the previous one, and lies close to the HCCA.

The sheared structure of Norbert and the proximity of drier air to 
the west of the system suggests that only modest near-term 
strengthening should be expected. However, the shear is forecast to 
weaken over the next few days while the system moves into a 
sufficiently moist environment over waters near 28C.  Despite these 
seemingly favorable conditions, there are mixed signals in the 
guidance regarding how much strengthening may occur.  There is also 
a large spread in some of the ensemble intensity guidance.  For 
example, the Google DeepMind ensemble has a spread at day 4 that 
ranges from 30 to 120 kt.  The HAFS-A keeps it a tropical storm 
through the forecast period.  The HAFS-B briefly makes it a category 
1 hurricane within the next 60 hours before weakening the system 
back to a low-end tropical storm by day 4-5.  The NHC intensity 
forecast is similar to the previous one, showing a slightly faster 
intensification in the first 48 hours, but then a slower rate of 
strengthening thereafter.  The NHC intensity forecast still lies on 
the higher end of the guidance envelope and calls for Norbert to 
reach hurricane strength by early next week.
